title: Spiritual joy in Christ is both Spirit’s fruit and believers’ commanded duty
source_text: XIV. Et certe gaudium illud spirituale quo fideles in Christo laetantur, quodque non potest esse sine certitudine de propria gratia, & ex ea sponte nascitur, non tantum est fructus quidam Spiritus Sancti optabilis, sed etiam fidelium officium. Gaudete, inquit Apostolus, in Domino semper; iterum dico, gaudete. Phil. 4. Et fidelium varia officia describens Rom. 12. inter alia ponit illud, Spe gaudentes.
pass_a_gloss: And certainly that spiritual joy with which believers rejoice in Christ—which cannot exist without certainty of one’s own grace and which springs spontaneously from it—is not only a desirable fruit of the Holy Spirit but also a duty of believers. Rejoice in the Lord always; again I say, rejoice (Phil. 4). And describing believers’ various duties in Romans 12, among other things he places this: rejoicing in hope.
pass_b_english: Joy in Christ requires certainty of grace and is both Spirit-fruit and commanded duty.
Philippians 4 and Romans 12 make rejoicing a standing office of the faithful.
